A.explanation: The product $\rho g$ has unit $\text{N m}^{-3}$, which is pressure per unit length, so it is too small by a factor of length to be a pressure.

B.explanation: For side length $l$, weight $\rho l^3 g$ divided by area $l^2$ gives $p = \rho g l$, the stated product.

C.explanation: Multiplying by face area $l^2$ gives $\rho g l^2$ with unit $\text{N m}^{-1}$, not pressure, because area should divide the weight not multiply it.

D.explanation: The product $\rho g$ times volume $V$ equals $\rho V g$, which is the weight force in $\text{N}$, not weight divided by area.

hints: Notice the cube presses with its weight, so start from $p = F/A$ where $F$ is the weight and $A$ is the area of the one face in contact.
Connect weight to density using $m = \rho V$, with cube volume $V = l^3$ and contact area $A = l^2$ if $l$ is the side length.
Simplify $p = \rho l^3 g / l^2$ and check which of the listed products of $g$, $\rho$, length, area or volume matches and has pressure unit $\text{Pa}$.
walkthrough: Identify the physics: pressure due to weight is $p = F/A = W/A$, where $A$ is the area of the cube face on the surface.
Write the weight from mass and free fall acceleration: $W = mg$, and write mass from density and volume: $m = \rho V$.
For a cube of side length $l$, volume is $V = l^3$ and contact area is $A = l^2$, so $p = \rho V g / A = \rho l^3 g / l^2$.
Simplify to $p = \rho g l$, which is the product of acceleration of free fall, density and side length. This is option B.
